day.text: Blair here, Hawk, Farm. I visited Drew and got no egg, so Drew is not Meowfia. My nest didn't change, and Ellis, you visited me. Drew, whoever gave you those 2 eggs, the Meowfia aren't you as far as I can tell.
day.note: I'm the Hawk and visited Drew, and got no egg, so Drew is not Meowfia. Sharing that to clear Drew and get the table moving.

day.text: Casey here, I'm the Tit, Farm. I visited Alex and guessed Pigeon, no egg, so Alex isn't a Pigeon. My nest didn't change. Alex, what did you do last night?

day.text: Alex here, Falcon, Farm. I visited Blair and saw they visited Drew, so that matches Blair's story. My nest didn't change. Casey, I'm not a Pigeon, so your guess on me was wrong. Drew, what gave you those 2 eggs, and who visited you?

day.note: Drew's Kookaburra claim doesn't explain a +2 gain, and Casey's Tit claim is still open. I'll press the egg counts without committing to a vote yet.

day.text: Drew, Kookaburra doesn't lay eggs on its own, so your +2 needs a source. I only saw Blair visit you. Who else gave you eggs? Casey, Tit vs Mouser, pick one and explain.
day.note: Drew's 2 eggs don't fit a Kookaburra visit and my Eagle check only shows Blair visiting Drew. Drew may be lying, or the eggs came from somewhere else. I'll press for Drew's and Casey's specifics without committing.

day.text: Alex: Agreed, a Kookaburra visit doesn't pay eggs, so Drew's +2 has no source yet. Drew, if you're confused, your Casey-is-Mouser read is unreliable too. Casey, I need one clear answer: did your Tit guess on me give an egg, and did you visit anyone else? Nobody throws until we have that.
day.note: Drew's +2 is still unexplained, and Drew's Kookaburra info is admittedly confused. I'll press Casey and Drew for a clear source rather than throw yet.

day.text: Casey: I'm the Tit, not a Mouser. I visited Alex, no egg, and I wasn't confused. Drew, if you were visited by Blair and gained 2, you're hiding a source. Drew is my lead for now, but I want more before anyone throws.
day.note: Drew's claim that I'm a Mouser is false; I'm a Tit and my dawn report was clean, so I wasn't confused. Drew's +2 has no source, which makes Drew the suspect. I'll say so and not throw yet.

day.text: Ellis: Agreed, nobody has explained Drew's +2 yet. Casey, did your Tit guess on Alex pay an egg, yes or no? If it didn't, the Tit claim doesn't help you.

day.text: Ellis: My visit to Drew is the only one I can vouch for, and Casey's +1 fits it. Drew, your Falcon read on Blair has no egg behind it either, so I'm not sure who's lying yet. No throw until someone's story holds up.
day.note: Casey's +1 fits my visit to Drew, so I shouldn't attack Casey's Eagle claim. I'll stay neutral and avoid calling CAW until the table has a clear target.

day.text: Alex: Roles are dealt fresh each round, so my Falcon, Turkey, and Hawk are three different rounds, not a shifting story. Casey's Tit and Eagle both happened in this game, but Casey still hasn't explained the eggs in the same role twice. I'm throwing at Casey.
day.note: Casey is trying to make my role changes look suspicious, but those were round-by-round deals. Casey's shifting Tit and Eagle claims are the real issue, so I'll throw a low card at Casey.

day.text: Blair: Drew's Falcon read on Blair has no egg behind it, and Drew is leading on points. I'm leaning Drew for the throw.
day.note: I'm Meowfia, so I want a Farm player eggsecuted. Drew leads on points and Drew's Falcon read has no egg support, so I'm pointing the table at Drew.

day.text: Drew: My Falcon fact is simple: no egg means Blair visited someone, and that's all it tells me. Leading on points doesn't make me Meowfia. I'm throwing at Casey with Alex.
day.note: Blair is turning on me because I lead on points. I'll state the one fact my Falcon gives, that no egg means Blair visited someone, and keep my throw on Casey.

day.text: Finley: Drew's Falcon read on Blair has no support, and Blair has denied it. I'm throwing at Drew.
day.note: Drew's Falcon claim has no egg behind it and is contradicted by Blair, so Drew is my best throw target. I'll throw a single Wild and keep my real cards.

Alex.note: As Hawk I visit to check for Meowfia. Ellis is the least-tested player, so I'll check them.

Blair.note: As the Sphinx I can name a farm role and learn that player. Picking Hawk, since a Hawk is the farm role best placed to expose cats.

Casey.note: I'm the Eagle, Farm. I'll visit Drew, the score leader, to learn their visitors and gain eggs for each.

Drew.note: As a Farm Falcon, I'll visit Blair to learn who they visited and possibly gain an egg if they visited no one.

Ellis.note: I'm Meowfia as the Floofer. Drew leads the scores at 19, and hugging Drew blocks whatever Farm role they have tonight.

Finley.note: I'm Farm as the Tit, and I'm behind on points. Pigeon is the most likely role to be in play, so I'll visit Ellis and guess Pigeon.

Alex.feeling: Tense and muddled: several players have shifting or contradictory claims, and the eggs don't line up cleanly yet.

Blair.feeling: Tense and muddled: the claims keep shifting and Casey and Drew are each accusing the other, so I'm hiding my Sphinx role while trying to steer the throw.

Casey.feeling: Tense and muddled: several players have shifting or unverifiable role claims, and the vote is split between Alex, Drew, and Finley.

Drew.feeling: Messy and contradictory: several players have shifted claims and egg counts don't line up, so I'm not confident who is lying.

Ellis.feeling: Tense and murky: Casey and Drew are at each other's throats over a Falcon claim and shifting roles, and I'm Meowfia with no partner I can identify, so I'm mostly trying to avoid drawing a throw.

Finley.feeling: Round 3 is messy: several players' claims contradict each other, and I can't yet tell who is lying, so I'm uneasy about the next throw.

Alex.note: Keeping the throw on Casey with a low card, S3.

Blair.note: I'm Meowfia and want a Farm player eliminated. Throwing at Drew, the leader on points, with two low cards.

Casey.note: Alex is my target after the shifting claims and pressure on me. I'll throw my Wild and a 5 for two votes while keeping my high cards.

Drew.note: I'm throwing at Casey, my main suspect, using the Wild and a 7 so my high cards stay safe.

Ellis.note: Drew leads the scores and is the most damaging Farm player to let win. I'll add one low card to the Drew throw, since Finley is already on it.

Finley.note: I'm sticking with Drew, the target I announced. I'll throw one Wild.

Alex.confusing: The Eagle and Floofer claims were hard to sort out, since players kept changing roles and it was unclear which visit reports could be trusted. Also, the confusion mechanic made some dawn reports unreliable.
Alex.fun: Catching Finley's contradiction in round 2 with my Turkey nest was satisfying, because my own unchanged egg count proved one player's visit claim false.
Alex.change: I'd make the dawn reports clearer about which visits paid eggs, so players spend less time arguing over claims that can't be checked.
Alex.regret: In round 1 I joined the throw on Drew, who was Farm, when Ellis the Floofer was the real Meowfia. I'd have pressed Ellis's and Casey's stories harder instead of following the crowd.

Blair.confusing: Hidden effects were hard to read from the table. A hugged or blocked visit silently blanks your egg check, so a "no egg" result can mean nothing at all.
Blair.fun: Round 1's mystery about Drew's unexplained +2 pulled the whole table into debate. Playing the Sphinx as a cat in round 3 and steering the vote from inside was also satisfying.
Blair.change: I would make blocked or hugged visits visible to the visitor, so a Hawk check that did nothing can't be mistaken for a clean Farm result.
Blair.regret: In round 1 I threw my vote at Casey, a Farm Tit, and never questioned Ellis, the Floofer who visited me and was the real Meowfia. Next time I'd check every visitor's claim against my own nest before voting.

Casey.confusing: The dawn egg logic was hard to track: a Hawk or Floofer visit could be hidden or blocked, so a "no egg" result didn't clear anyone. Round 3's Eagle +1 was also easy to misread as a Casey-specific story.
Casey.fun: Round 2, when Finley's Eagle claim collapsed and then switched to Floofer, the table caught the lie and threw Finley out, and the Farm side won that round.
Casey.change: I'd make it clearer when a visit is blocked or hugged, so players can tell "no egg" from "no visit" without guesswork.
Casey.regret: My round 1 throw at Drew was wrong: Drew was Farm and Ellis, the real Meowfia, was never challenged. I'd have pressed Ellis's visit story harder instead of following Blair's lead.

Drew.confusing: The confusion from my confused Kookaburra report made my Mouser read on Casey unreliable, and I never found out where my +2 in round 1 came from. Nest changes with no visible source were the hardest part to reason about.
Drew.fun: Round 2 was a good table fight: Finley claimed Eagle, then Floofer, and the whole table turned on the contradiction until the day ended on a CAW vote.
Drew.change: I would make a confused player's report say which of its numbers are wrong, so everyone knows what to trust. As it stands, a confused player can't tell which of their own claims to stand behind.
Drew.regret: In round 3 I threw at Casey, a Farm Eagle, while Blair was the Sphinx and the real Meowfia. I should have backed the throw at Blair once Blair pushed me, since that cost me the round and the lead.

Ellis.confusing: The Floofer hug: a hugged visitor's "no egg" report proves nothing, and nobody could tell whether a hug had blocked a visit. Confused reports and Eagle or Tit claims from different rounds also made it hard to check who was lying.
Ellis.fun: Finley's Eagle claim fell apart when Alex's Turkey nest stayed unchanged, and the table turned on Finley within one beat. Watching the egg counts settle the claims was the most satisfying part.
Ellis.change: I would make the dawn reports state whether a visitor was hugged or blocked, so players can check claims against egg counts. Confused players would still be hidden.
Ellis.regret: I never used my Meowfia teammate, Blair, who was the Sphinx in round 3. I should have found them early and agreed on which Farm player to target, instead of voting with the table each time.

Finley.confusing: Egg sources were hard to trace, since several roles only pay out when visited and claims often couldn't be checked against the eggs. Confused players' reports also made it unclear who to trust.
Finley.fun: Round 2 was the most fun, when I was the Meowfia Floofer, bluffing an Eagle claim and then retracting it under pressure. Watching the table build a case against me was tense.
Finley.change: I would make the Eagle and Owl visitor reports clearer, so players can verify claims without guessing whose egg came from where.
Finley.regret: In round 2 I made up an Eagle visit and then changed to Floofer, which made me look like a liar. I should have stuck to one story and kept my vote small. In round 3 I threw at Drew, who was Farm, when Blair was the real Meowfia Sphinx; I should have looked harder at Blair.

review.title: Hugs and Shifting Claims
review.headline: Drew led by a mile, got eggsecuted twice, and still won.
review.summary: Round 1 ended with Farm throwing at Drew, a confused Kookaburra whose odd +2 looked like a Meowfia lie, while the lone cat Ellis hid and won. Round 2 was an easy Farm win once Finley's fake Eagle claim collapsed against Alex's Turkey nest. Drew banked 12 points that round and was never caught up. Round 3 saw the two cats, Blair and Ellis, pile onto the leader Drew and win. Drew still finished first.

rounds.recap: Ellis was the only Meowfia (Floofer) and hugged Blair, which did nothing. Drew's Kookaburra was confused, so he gained 2 eggs with no source and named Casey as Mouser, which was false. The table threw at Drew, who was Farm, and the cat won without being suspected.

Finley, the Floofer, claimed Eagle and visited a Turkey who showed no visitor. Alex's unchanged nest disproved the claim. Finley then switched to Floofer, and everyone threw at Finley. Drew's high throws banked 12 points.

Blair (Sphinx) and Ellis (Floofer) did not know each other but both aimed at Drew, the score leader. Farm split between Casey, Alex and Drew over muddy Eagle and Falcon claims. Drew took the most votes, Farm lost, and the cats scored.

highlights.text: Alex's Turkey with an unchanged nest killed Finley's false Eagle visit claim in one line.
Finley retracted the Eagle claim and admitted to being the Floofer, a desperate and useless flip.
Drew's confusion produced a false Mouser read and an unexplained +2, and the table eggsecuted the innocent Kookaburra.
Two cats who didn't know each other both went for Drew, the score leader, and won.

confusions.what: Said Drew's +2 couldn't come from a Kookaburra, without considering that confusion changes the egg report.
Called Drew's +2 unsourced even though Finley's own Eagle report showed Blair as the only visitor. Drew's eggs were a confusion artifact.
Said Alex as Turkey 'gains an egg per visitor' and used that against Finley. That is correct. But Casey also treated Ellis's Owl as 'blocking' the Tit visit, which isn't a rule.
Said Casey's Tit visit never paid anyone, then used that to doubt Drew's Eagle count, which was right.
Argued Drew's Falcon claim conflicted with Blair visiting Alex, though a Falcon only learns that Blair visited someone.
Thought Casey's Owl claim in round 2 was this round's Owl claim, and said Alex's and Finley's visits to Ellis conflicted when both can visit the same player.
Said Drew's Falcon report was unsupported by Blair, but Falcon dawn text was simply blank in the report, not wrong.
Claimed the Falcon visit proves Blair visited someone, but the Falcon was hugged so the result was likely blank.

worked: Alex's Turkey gave a checkable, hard fact in round 2 that exposed a false visit claim. Egg-change nest sizes make that kind of cross-check possible.
Confusion on a Kookaburra in round 1 made an honest player look like a liar. That is a good source of fair, tense doubt.
Meowfia not knowing each other, plus a leader to target, made the round 3 cat win feel earned rather than coordinated.
The ties-go-to-Meowfia and consolation rules gave Finley a real reason to throw a Wild at Blair in round 2.
problems: Snowballing: Drew banked 12 in round 2 by throwing two 6s on a sure win, and was 4 points clear after. A winning throw banking full value rewards the safest-looking vote, and the others could not catch up. Consider capping banked points per round or hiding the leader's lead.
Most night results are silent or no-effect (hugs on Hawk and Tit 'no effect', Hawk and Tit 'no egg'). Players had little to reason from and spent days repeating the same unexplained +1 or +2.

Vote logic is weak: in round 1 the table threw at an unsourced +2 and ignored that confusion exists. Confused reports are not marked as such to the table, so false reads cause dead-end votes. Maybe give confusion a visible tell.

Falcon and Kookaburra reports gave little. The hugged Falcon in round 3 learned nothing, and the claim was then treated as a lie. Hugged outcomes should show a visible signal or the role is easily framed.
Players kept saying 'no throws yet' then all threw anyway, and the CAW rule ended days early. Beats 3 and 4 repeated statements and added little new information.
